messages:
Anya: heads-up — noticed a persistent drop in eu-west-1 warm pool counts over the last 3 hours, while queue depth is steady. SLOs for 99p tail are creeping up. grafana: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/infra/warm-pool?orgId=1&var-region=eu-west-1 :thinking_face:
Mike: hmm, are those nodes retiring or failing readiness probes? any restart spikes?
Anya: no big restarts. warm-pool-count panel shows a steady -1 every ~10min. autoscaler commit for eu-west is still at desired=40.
Jamal: can you paste the prom query you used? I want to correlate with kube events and nvml errors.
Anya: sure — here's the query I used:
```
sum by(pod) (increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="infra-warm",container="warm-agent"}[1h]))
```
It returns near-zero. but this one shows node removal vs scale desired:
```
sum(kube_node_status_allocatable{resource="nvidia.com/gpu"}) by (kubernetes_io_hostname)
```
shows nodes dropping at odd intervals.
Mike: could be a cloud-side preemption / maintenance. Any spot eviction logs?
Jamal: I pulled kube-events for the timeframe — seeing repeated taint injection on some nodes: `node.kubernetes.io/unreachable:NoSchedule` but not full cordon. also some kubelet disconnects with TLS handshake errors. snippet from node logs:
```
Mar 19 10:12:05 node-23 kubelet[1234]: E0319 10:12:05.123456    1234 kubelet_node_status.go:123] Error posting node status: TLS handshake timeout
Mar 19 10:12:06 node-23 kubelet[1234]: W0319 10:12:06.123456    1234 eviction_manager.go:345] eviction manager: failed to remove pod: network error
```
Anya: interesting — I also see autoscaler picking new nodes but warmup-agent fails liveness checks and never transitions to ready, so pool count decreases.
InfraBot: [alert] infra:warm-pool-eu-west decreased below 20 (current: 17) — fired 1797654300. Alert doc: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/INF/Warm+Pool+Alerts
Mike: can someone run a focused probe: SSH to one of the recently-created nodes and check dmesg + nvml? I can script a quick check.
Jamal: on it. I found a recurring kernel OOM-killer trace on node-27 right at the warmup time. nv_peer_mem not present in the kernel logs. Could be driver mismatch after node image patching.
Anya: that would explain liveness failures. we've been rolling node-images in eu-west last night (image-build-2026.03.18). Did we bump the nvidia driver there?
Mike: yes—image-build included nvidia-driver 530.14.2. Legacy warmup VM images were pinned to 525.x until now. rollout notes: https://deploys.redwood.company/changes/2026-03-18-image-build
Jamal: propose immediate mitigation: pin warm-pool to previous image via nodeSelector + create a rollback pool, then trigger rolling canary of driver upgrade to a few dedicated test nodes. Also adjust alert to distinguish warm-pool readiness vs desired mismatch.
Anya: I can create a temporary taint/toleration rule to keep the old nodes for warm-pool, but need infra approval for image rollback.
SRE Oncall: agreed — prioritize SLO stability. Anya, open a quick PR to the infra-autoscaler config with the nodeSelector override and set warm-pool min=30 to avoid further dips while we investigate. I'll take ownership of the rollback request with platform leads.
Mike: for observability follow-ups: add a panel showing `sum by(node) (time() - kubelet_runtime_state)`? maybe better: correlate `kubelet_runtime_operations_duration_seconds` to see hangups. Also add kernel OOM count per node.
Jamal: I put a short prom query to detect the exact symptom — add as alert rule maybe with longer evaluation window to avoid noise:
```
rule: warm_pool_readiness_gap
expr: max_over_time(kube_pod_status_ready{namespace="infra-warm"}[30m]) < bool 1 and sum(kube_node_status_allocatable{resource="nvidia.com/gpu"}) < desired_gpu_count
for: 10m
```
This should catch cases where nodes exist but warm agents never become ready.
Anya: logging note — we need the warm-agent to emit early-stage failure reason on start (driver mismatch), currently it fails silently. I'll file a tiny prod-bug to add clearer error logs.
SRE Oncall: next steps: 1) Mike to run nvml/kernel checks on flagged nodes (in progress). 2) Anya to open PR for nodeSelector override and increase warm-pool min. 3) I will escalate image rollback with platform. 4) Jamal to add the readiness-gap alert and temp dashboard panel. Target: revert warm-pool to >30 within 1 hour.
Mike: nvml check preliminary — `nvidia-smi` hangs on node-27, kernel reports module mismatch. collecting output and will paste.
Anya: thanks. ping me when the PR is up and I'll apply. :thumbsup:
InfraBot: action logged: incident-1797654321 created, priority P2, assignees: Anya, Mike, Jamal, SRE Oncall. Link: https://incidents.redwood.company/1797654321
Jamal: added the temp grafana panel (panel id 8932) to the infra/warm dashboard showing readiness-gap and kernel-oom spikes. folks, check it for false positives and tell me if we should lower the for: window.
SRE Oncall: status update in 20m or when warm-pool >30. thanks everyone.
